questions.q: Why can't a question like 'which services are still running an end-of-life runtime' be answered by manual audit at an organization with hundreds of services?
options: The question is unanswerable in principle, even with a scorecard
Terraform state files already track this information automatically
Any single team can answer it correctly just by checking its own services
A manual audit across that many services, spread across many teams, goes stale again almost immediately and no one person can see the whole picture
questions.explain: At real scale, a manual survey can't keep up with how fast new services ship and old ones change, and no individual team has visibility into every other team's services.

questions.q: In Backstage's Tech Insights plugin, what is a fact retriever?
options: A component that collects one concrete piece of data about every catalog entity, such as a pinned runtime version or a scan result
A manual report a team lead fills out quarterly
The UI widget that renders the final scorecard grid
A Terraform module used to provision new infrastructure
questions.explain: Fact retrievers gather concrete, per-entity data points -- a Node.js version, whether a scan workflow exists, an on-call owner field -- that checks then evaluate.

questions.q: What does a check do with the data a fact retriever collects?
options: It deletes the fact after one use to save storage
It evaluates the fact against a threshold and produces a pass/fail result, such as 'runtime is not end-of-life'
It automatically fixes the underlying problem without any human involvement
It sends the raw fact directly to a ticketing system
questions.explain: A check is a rule applied to a fact -- comparing a retrieved value against an expected threshold to produce a simple pass or fail.

questions.q: What does a scorecard actually show once checks run across the whole catalog?
options: A single aggregate score for the entire company with no per-service detail
Only the services owned by the platform team itself
A grid where every row is a service, every column is a check, and every cell is a pass or fail -- surfacing patterns across hundreds of services at a glance
A list of every commit made to every repository in the last year
questions.explain: The grid format is what makes org-wide patterns -- like a cluster of services still on a deprecated runtime -- visible in minutes instead of requiring a team-by-team survey.

questions.q: Why does a Tech Insights check depend on the catalog from Lesson 5 being accurate?
options: It does not depend on the catalog at all; checks run independently of any entity data
A fact retriever only produces a correct result if it's reading real entity data, such as a repo the catalog correctly points at and an owner field that's actually filled in
Checks only read data directly from a ticketing system, never from the catalog
The catalog is only needed for software templates, not for scorecards
questions.explain: A fact retriever's output is only as good as the catalog data it reads from. If an entity's repo link or metadata is wrong, the fact -- and therefore the check -- is wrong too.
